title: Why You're Broke on a Good Salary (Lifestyle Creep Math)

lines.say: Good salary, and still broke by the end of the month?
You're not bad with money. Your spending grew with your pay. It has a name: lifestyle creep.
Here's the math of how a raise disappears, and the one rule that stops it.
First, where the raises went.

scene.label: Four years of raises
scene.sub: a month: take-home went from $3,200 to $4,400

lines.cap: Our example got a raise every year. Over four years, take-home went from $3,200 a month to $4,400. $1,200 more, every month.
lines.say: Our example got a raise every year. Over four years, take-home went from thirty-two hundred a month to forty-four hundred. Twelve hundred more, every month.

scene.head: Where the extra $1,200 a month went

lines.say: Here's where it went.
A nicer apartment, three hundred more.
A newer car payment, two fifty more.
Takeout and delivery, two hundred more.
Subscriptions and apps, sixty.

lines.cap: And everything just a bit nicer: $390.
lines.say: And everything just a bit nicer, three ninety.

scene.label: Saved from four years of raises

lines.say: Savings from four years of raises? Zero. Same stress. Nicer stuff.

scene.text: Spending ratchets up easily. It almost never comes back down.

lines.say: And here's the catch. Spending ratchets up easily, but it almost never comes back down. A new lease, or a car payment, locks it in for years.
The fix is the half-raise rule.

scene.text: Every raise: half to your life, half to your future.

lines.say: Every time you get a raise, half goes to your life, and half goes straight to savings or debt, before you ever see it.

lines.cap: So each $300 raise means $150 more to enjoy, and $150 saved automatically. You still feel every raise.
lines.say: So each three hundred dollar raise means a hundred fifty more to enjoy, and a hundred fifty saved automatically. You still feel every raise.

lines.cap: Year one: $150 a month. Year two: $300. By year four: $600 a month.
lines.say: Year one, a hundred fifty a month. Year two, three hundred. By year four, six hundred a month.

scene.label: After four years at 4%
scene.sub: from money you never got used to spending

lines.cap: After four years at 4%, that's about $19,096. From money you never got used to spending.
lines.say: After four years, at four percent, that's about nineteen thousand dollars. From money you never got used to spending.
Already crept? Do a creep audit this week.

scene.head: THE CREEP AUDIT
items: Pull a statement from 3 years ago
Compare it to last month, line by line
Mark each increase: worth it, or not?
Cut one, and automate the savings

lines.say: Here's how.
Pull a statement from three years ago.
Compare it to last month, line by line.
Mark every increase. Worth it, or not?
Then cut one that's not worth it, and send that money to savings automatically.
